> **A wall is a physical assembly. A boundary is a performance relationship that may pass through many assemblies.**
The phrase “this wall is the envelope” hides too much.
The computational model therefore treats boundaries as first-class semantic systems rather than as generic properties attached to one wall object.
A cavity wall may physically contain facing masonry, cavity, insulation, structural inner leaf, air-control layer, lining, window, closer, seals and lintel.
One component can contribute to several boundaries. One boundary can pass through several components. This many-to-many relationship is the reason boundary identity matters.
A boundary can be understood as a connected semantic graph or surface network independent of any one CAD-layer convention.
The exact geometry may be a line, surface or region depending on the boundary and method.
Only applicable roles should be instantiated.
Where is rain shed? Where can water enter? Where is it intercepted, drained and allowed to dry?
What defines the insulated enclosure? Where are the openings, junctions and bridges?
What provides primary air control? How do openings, junctions and penetrations maintain continuity?
What wetting paths exist, where is vapour resistance intended and how can the assembly dry?
This remains assembly-specific; it should never collapse into a universal “vapour barrier” rule.
What separating or cavity-control function applies, where does it continue, what penetrates it and how is performance reinstated?
Which spaces require separation, what are the direct and flanking paths, and how do openings, penetrations, mass and decoupling affect them?
What constitutes the secure perimeter and which openings or interfaces control access?
Where can pests enter or travel, and how are vents, cavities and drains protected without defeating another boundary function?
is not a complete air-boundary model.
The boundary describes continuity and transition across the enclosure, not merely the material used in one field condition.
This is analogous to structural load-path continuity.
A routinely removable layer should not casually become the sole carrier of a critical slow-building function expected to survive its removal.
If the project requires the air boundary to remain intact during routine lining removal, that state should be rejected or create an unresolved obligation.
A service penetration is not merely a hole.
The same physical hole can create very different obligations depending on which boundaries and structural conditions it crosses.
The current compiler already uses this principle: selected service penetrations generate boundary-reinstatement duties rather than disappearing between service and envelope abstractions.
A window does more than puncture a wall.
The opening therefore creates a **bundle of obligations** across several domains.
This aligns with the architectural pattern **Permanent Opening / Replaceable Window**: the long-lived opening owns enduring geometry and the shorter-lived window occupies that interface.
This is more useful than pretending each discipline owns an isolated detail.
The semantic model should expose the correct geometric query, specialist method or external evidence required for the latter rather than claiming that topology proves performance.
Water requires more than continuity.
Relevant facts can include exposure, protected side, fall direction, overlap, drip, weep and cavity collection path.
The current Reference House roof model already derives catchments and ensures roof drainage remains directed outward rather than silently reversing toward the courtyard.
Avoid slogans such as “always install a vapour barrier” or “every cavity must be ventilated”.
Air leakage commonly concentrates at transitions: floor and roof edges, openings, penetrations and service entries.
Relevant evidence can include continuity review, supported detail families, pre-closure inspection and final airtightness testing where appropriate.
A coloured field-wall layer without its transitions is not a complete air-boundary model.
The compiler need not become an acoustic engine merely to know that a junction or penetration has created an acoustic obligation.
Fire is especially unsafe to compress into `fire-rated = true`.
A supported fire claim needs its actual function, assembly/evidence, conditions, openings and penetrations, and field of application.
Novel or project-specific fire engineering remains external unless a bounded method has genuinely been admitted.
Transitions may be more valuable than generic field details because failures and conflicting duties concentrate at junctions.
Replacement can intentionally open a boundary without destroying the architectural strategy.
This lets replacement become a declared state transition rather than an unmodelled demolition event.
These evidence phases attach to the same semantic boundary system while remaining different kinds of evidence.

Ventilation competes with airtightness. Drainage openings compete with pest exclusion. Acoustic decoupling can compete with structural restraint. Removable access can compete with fire/acoustic closure. Vapour resistance can compete with drying.

The present compiler represents weather, air, thermal and moisture boundary systems independently across the Reference House; turns openings and selected service crossings into explicit transition/reinstatement obligations; derives roof catchments and drainage relationships from canonical geometry; and prevents critical slow-envelope functions from migrating accidentally onto routinely removable layers.
It does **not** prove U-values, thermal bridges, condensation safety, fire resistance, acoustic performance, airtightness or whole-envelope physical adequacy.
Those remain external methods/evidence until a bounded technical method is deliberately admitted.
A compile result needs a named normative environment.
> **A named, immutable, versioned representation of the external normative environment against which defined claims are compiled.**
It should not become a container for architectural preference, software capability, product choice and project facts.
The external normative environment: jurisdiction, applicable regulatory snapshot, building/work class, transition basis, selected compliance route and incorporated standards/methods.
What Metamorph Compiler legitimately knows how to represent or establish: supported geometry, semantic relationships, method families and proof envelopes.
The selected design language, such as G-01, with its own architectural authority.
Facts and requirements particular to the job: site, ground evidence, climate/exposure, brief, budget, programme and chosen performance targets.
The separation matters because a grammar deviation, an unsupported technical condition and a legal failure are not the same kind of fact even if each blocks one workflow.
> **“Use the latest rules” is not a valid target-selection algorithm.**
A target needs enough provenance to explain why its regulatory basis applies to the project being evaluated.
Which functional requirements apply: structure, fire, moisture, ventilation, sound, sanitation, energy, access, overheating, electrical safety and others as relevant.
Useful metadata includes source title, issuer, identifier, edition, publication/effective dates, supersession and authoritative source location.
Planning and Building Regulations are different legal and decision systems.

A real project may also need to represent development-plan policy, conservation-area constraints, listed status, permitted-development conditions, local design codes or site-specific planning obligations.
Those should not be folded into the building-control target merely because both affect whether a project can proceed.
Their authorities remain distinct.
Submission packaging, contacts, naming conventions and review correspondence belong to a downstream process profile rather than the normative target itself.
This preserves the possibility of alternative compliant routes and prevents guidance text from being silently promoted into the legal requirement itself.
The standards-ingestion architecture should follow the authoritative ecosystem rather than be invented prematurely.
Suppose one guidance edition is implemented as machine method `M-3`.
This distinction applies equally to calculation methods, table transcriptions and formalised interpretation rules.
Where authoritative interpretation remains ambiguous, expose the ambiguity or require competent determination rather than manufacturing determinism.
The computational system therefore tracks proof routes rather than pretending one encoded path exhausts all legal means of compliance.
A target or target-linked method set may cover only part of the wider regulatory environment.
Project requirements derived from Ovid’s House may be stricter than regulation and should remain independently reportable.
A pattern reference or House Kernel provenance never upgrades architectural authority into regulation, engineering or product evidence.
Every consequential compile should retain the configuration that gave the result.
A result without this context is difficult to interpret or reproduce.
Once a release claims Target T, the meaning of T should not silently change.
If source guidance or an encoded implementation changes, create a new target/method identity, preserve the earlier one and decide explicitly whether an existing project needs to migrate.
> **What exactly was this conclusion compiled against?**
The present Metamorph Compiler does not implement a release-grade England building-control target.

Its current regulatory example is intentionally much smaller: a versioned private-stair numeric method compares controlled Reference House stair geometry with a selected Approved Document K guidance family while explicitly refusing to call the result whole-building Building Regulations compliance.
That bounded example demonstrates the target/method distinction without implying a general regulations engine.

A release-grade England target would require substantially more: applicability mapping, exact source/transition provenance, validated method implementations, standards/licensing strategy, known-pass/known-fail regression cases and competent regulatory review.
A computational building model becomes trustworthy only when its claims can be traced to evidence of the right scope.
A folder containing drawings, calculations, product data and certificates is not yet an evidence system. A future reader also needs to know:
The evidence architecture therefore treats provenance as part of the model rather than decorative metadata around it.
The obligation says **what needs to be established**. Evidence says **what supports the conclusion**. The result records the present epistemic state.
Keeping those separate prevents an uploaded document from being mistaken for a proven proposition merely because it exists.
Facts derived directly from a controlled semantic source: identity, topology, geometry, quantities or other deterministic projections.
Results from a stated analytical or numeric method, with method identity, inputs, applicability and assumptions.
Fire, acoustic, structural, weather or other test/classification results covering a bounded assembly and field of application.
Declarations, installation conditions, technical literature or other manufacturer evidence whose authority and scope remain explicit.
Topographic survey, ground investigation, existing-building survey, utility survey or other real-site information.
Measured bearing, concealed-work record, fixing spacing, product identity or other observations of the physical building.
Airtightness, ventilation flow, electrical test, functional water test and similar completion evidence.
Approval, certificate or planning decision where relevant. This is evidence about a legal process, not native compiler proof.
> **What exactly does this establish?**
Change a scoped parameter and evidence inheritance may disappear. This is why a property such as `wall-is-fire-safe = true` is an inadequate model.
**Family-level evidence** supports a reusable design envelope: a tested wall, engineered joist table or certified window family.
**Occurrence-level evidence** supports a particular instance: the selected materials were installed, a bearing was measured, a fire stop was inspected, a terminal was commissioned.
A design-stage result may therefore legitimately rely on family evidence while physical conformance remains a later obligation.
The distinction prevents a tested family from silently proving installation quality and prevents an installation photograph from being mistaken for technical design evidence.
Evidence can have its own state independently of the obligation result.
An old calculation can remain in the record without governing the current building state.
Some evidence cannot exist at design stage.
A useful evidence architecture therefore distinguishes what is **due now** from what is legitimately **due later**.
A future obligation is legitimate where its method, responsible party, due phase/hold point and failure response are already clear.
This allows compilation to generate an evidence plan without pretending design information can prove future workmanship.
Evidence should declare the facts it depends on.
Assumptions should be structured facts rather than hidden caveats.
Copyrighted standards can be referenced without reproducing protected text.
A `NOT_APPLICABLE` result should be explainable for the same reason.
“Engineer approved” or “building control accepted” is too coarse to act as evidence architecture.
Avoid invented confidence percentages unless a real probabilistic method exists.
Specific epistemic language is more useful than pseudo-precision.
Supports the represented design: geometry, calculations, specifications, selected families and product/system evidence.
Supports the claim that construction corresponds sufficiently to the design: identity, measurement, inspection, test and commissioning.
Records later stewardship: maintenance, failure, replacement, alteration and measured performance.
One building record can contain all three without treating them as interchangeable.
A change can carry an explicit impact derived from dependencies.
The dependency graph—not memory—should decide what must be revisited.
England’s higher-risk-building regime provides useful precedent for information architecture: version control, controlled change, compliance evidence, construction control and as-built records.
This allows the record to preserve traceability even where an artefact is confidential, licensed, security-sensitive or stored outside the public repository.
Do not create one obligation per screw.
Useful scopes may include building, system, assembly family, representative sample, occurrence or critical interface.
A tolerance strategy already describes incoming condition, datum, adjustment, remediation threshold and verification.
The target is the **smallest intelligible evidence set that proves the things worth proving**.
One evidence graph can support different readers.
Isolation, maintenance, replacement and emergency information.
Service routes, IDs, access/replacement method and compatible components.
Calculations, boundaries/interfaces, assumptions, deviations and evidence scope.
Requirement-by-requirement evidence, referenced drawings, standards, decisions and commissioning results.
Different projections retain one building identity.
Given the same source model, compiler version, methods/targets, datasets and accepted external evidence, deterministic portions of compilation should reproduce the same result.
Traceability should survive even when the underlying artefact cannot be redistributed.

The present compiler demonstrates the critical small-scale mechanism: obligations can carry scoped evidence; evidence applied outside scope can be rejected; source changes can stale dependent evidence without invalidating unrelated evidence; and accepted external determination remains distinguishable from native machine result.
> **The program should compile a habitat.**
The ambition is therefore not “draw a house, then run checks”. It is:
> **Author a building inside a bounded semantic system in which important consequences are part of the act of authoring.**
The compiler should operate on meaningful building entities rather than generic meshes alone.
A window may know which permanent opening it occupies, which boundaries it transforms, what replacement path it needs and which technical obligations arise at its perimeter.
A maintenance task may know its target, approach path, working position and withdrawal route.
This is not prescribed syntax. It illustrates the level of meaning required for computation to reason about architecture rather than merely surfaces.
Move a wall and more than a polygon may change. Depending on what the model actually knows, the change can affect:
A useful diagnostic explains the broken relationships rather than merely colouring the geometry red.
The long-term interface ambition is to move complexity into the system rather than demanding it from every author.

A useful test is whether someone comfortable manipulating a house in a game-like spatial interface could explore supported designs without first learning BIM authoring conventions, structural analysis software and every encoded dimensional rule.
That user is not thereby made legally or professionally competent. The point is the division of labour:
**interactive authoring environment + semantic building model + compiler + versioned methods/targets + evidence and production outputs**.
A 3D model is one view of that system, not the system itself.
The system may support a declared architectural grammar governing relationships among rooms, heights, openings, axes, bays, circulation, hierarchy and composition.
Three rule classes should remain distinct.

Conditions that must hold inside the represented supported domain: source integrity, topology closure, declared boundary continuity, selected method applicability and other genuinely deterministic requirements.
Conditions belonging to a selected architectural language: hierarchy, relational dimensions, opening families, alignments and other architectural commitments.
They are authored cultural/design rules, not laws of nature.
Conditions that can be assessed without becoming binary truth: economy, daylight quality, degree of symmetry, circulation efficiency, material use, maintenance burden, views or proportional fit.
Structure belongs in the semantic model even when capacity remains external engineering work.
This allows the compiler to expose missing supports, impossible reactions or unowned interruptions without pretending to replace structural engineering.
See [Structural Semantics](structural-semantics.md).
A wall is not one environmental Boolean.
The computational model therefore treats boundaries as semantic systems with continuity, transitions, penetrations, terminations and evidence rather than simply colouring one CAD layer “envelope”.
See [Boundary Semantics](boundary-semantics.md).
A design never compiles against “the rules” in the abstract.

A **compiler target** describes a named external normative environment such as jurisdiction, applicable regulatory snapshot, transitional basis, building/work classification, selected compliance route and referenced standards.
This separation prevents a stylistic preference, an unsupported technical condition and a legal failure from acquiring the same authority merely because each can block a workflow.
See [Compiler Targets](compiler-targets.md).
The central computational abstraction is an **obligation**: a proposition that must be resolved because of a represented relationship, external requirement or selected project commitment.
See [Validity and Obligations](validity-and-obligations.md) and [Evidence and Provenance](evidence-and-provenance.md).
Authors should not have to maintain those as duplicated checklists.
> **Obligations belong to composed building relationships, not to duplicated checklists attached to labels.**
See [Interface Obligation Bundles](interface-obligation-bundles.md).
A useful compile result is inspectable. Another person should be able to answer:
Compilation proves propositions about **the represented model, under declared assumptions, within a stated supported domain**.
It does not prove that the physical building matches the model.
Ground conditions, substitutions, construction tolerances, installation quality, concealed changes, commissioning results and later alterations may all remain external facts.
Several project principles concern relationships that can sometimes be formalised.
A trustworthy compiler should not support arbitrary architecture merely because it can draw it.
> **Unsupported is not invalid. Unsupported is also not proven.**
See [Supported Domain](supported-domain.md).
Stable semantic identity can outlive first construction.

A later alteration can in principle expose which permanent fabric, interfaces, boundaries and structural relationships change; which evidence becomes stale; which target applies; and what new proof is required.
If software is allowed to make consequential claims, its own behaviour must remain inspectable.

Semantic building representation, BIM, machine-readable information requirements, automated compliance checking, ontology-based reasoning, parametric design and generative planning are established fields.
The computational track therefore makes no novelty claim merely because it combines architecture and software.

> **Can a deliberately bounded, architecturally opinionated domestic design system represent enough shared architectural meaning that consequential changes propagate coherently, invalid states fail clearly and evidence remains scoped—without pretending to automate the whole building?**

The present Metamorph Compiler implements a bounded chain through plan semantics, qualitative structural topology, service topology and registered crossings, envelope/boundary obligations, selected numeric methods and deterministic inspection outputs.

It does **not** currently establish structural capacity, building-physics performance, fire adequacy, acoustic adequacy, MEP sizing, whole-building regulatory compliance or a general-purpose technical-family library.
A product page or technical manual can be useful evidence without becoming proof of the whole assembly, room or building around it.

The Mapei **Mapeguard WP System**, centred on Mapeguard WP 200, provides a concrete example of how House Kernel can scope real manufacturer evidence: identify exactly what the source supports, preserve the system relationships on which that support depends, and keep all other architectural and technical obligations separate.
This is an evidence-modelling example, not a product endorsement or permanent Reference House specification.
The example uses public Mapei UK material current to the recorded source set.
Supports the identity and intended role of the adhesive in bonding and sealing overlaps and compatible system accessories.
This is particularly valuable evidence because it describes dependencies and installation sequence rather than simply advertising a product.
It establishes conditions concerning substrate preparation, bonding, overlaps, junction strips, corner pieces, pipe collars, drain treatment and compatible finish adhesives within the cited system.
Where a real project relies on an ETA, DoP or another formal assessment, the exact document and revision actually relied upon must become part of the project evidence set.
An assessment identifier by itself is not proof that an installed bathroom satisfies the complete system.
This is useful because it turns a vague instruction such as “waterproof the bathroom” into a network of traceable product/system conditions.
Those remain separate obligations and evidence questions.
> **External evidence becomes more trustworthy when its authority is narrowed to what it actually supports.**
Three evidence levels should not collapse into one another.
This can be supported by product technical data.
This depends on several products and their relationship.
That additionally requires physical/as-built evidence.
**manufacturer system evidence is potentially applicable subject to the exact cited technical documents, detail geometry and installation conditions.**
Still unresolved are floor falls, structural openings, the exact drain, physical installation and any project-specific access or compliance obligations.
That separation is the useful result.
Changing only the pipe collar can stale the penetration-specific system evidence while leaving unrelated field-membrane or corner evidence current.
> **Manufacturer applicability and project acceptability are different validity dimensions.**
Instead it asks whether the proposed replacement carries enough evidence to discharge the same scoped obligations.
This preserves commodity replaceability where it is real without pretending interfaces are generic when they are not.
The field membrane is necessary but insufficient.
> **Evidence dependencies are relationships, not merely document attachments on objects.**
A PDF stored against “Bathroom 01” is not enough.
Exact source identity and revision should be retained in any real project evidence set rather than relying on these general references alone.
A CAD model is commonly organised around objects and geometry. That is insufficient for Ovid’s House because one piece of building can participate in several systems simultaneously.

An external wall may bound a room, support a floor, carry several environmental boundaries, contain an opening, exclude routine services, receive an attachment datum, separate sound and create future maintenance obligations.
The formal model is therefore best understood as a **multi-view semantic graph with stable identity**, from which geometry, analytical views and human outputs can be derived.
Three layers should remain distinct.
The authoritative description of represented architectural intent and selected physical systems: meaningful entities, facts and relationships authored or selected by the design process.
Purpose-specific projections such as structural, service, boundary, quantity, maintenance, obligation and geometric views.
Human- and machine-facing artefacts such as plans, sections, schedules, calculations, semantic registers, IFC mappings, quantities, proof manifests and publication graphics.
A drawing is therefore a view of the source model, not the ontology of the building.
Every meaningful entity needs stable identity across views and regeneration.
A window appearing in plan geometry, a boundary transition, a quantity schedule, a replacement sequence and a later alteration should remain the same semantic occurrence.
Identity should be stable where the entity remains conceptually the same and should change where the entity itself is replaced rather than merely edited.
These families describe semantic roles; they do not prescribe programming classes.
Relevant entities include building, storey, space, room, circulation space, void, courtyard, external space and maintenance/working/withdrawal volumes.
Relevant entities include assembly, element, layer, component, opening, finish, fastener, seal, cover, replaceable unit and permanent-fabric element.
Relevant entities include structural element, support, bearing, connection, action/load, stability system and foundation/ground support condition.
See [Structural Semantics](structural-semantics.md).
A boundary should have first-class identity rather than being inferred from visible materials.
Relevant entities include boundary, boundary segment, transition, penetration, opening, seal, drainage path and failure path.
See [Boundary Semantics](boundary-semantics.md).
Relevant entities include system, network, node, port, route segment, source, sink, equipment, isolator, distribution point and discharge point.
Relevant entities include interface, joint, datum, tolerance envelope, adjustment mechanism, fixing interface, release mechanism, movement allowance and remediation threshold.
An interface can create structural, movement, tolerance, boundary, removal and inspection obligations at once.

Relevant entities include permanence class, service-life band, replacement unit, maintenance task, inspection task, replacement sequence, access path, working position, withdrawal path, commissioning test and change event.

Relevant entities include requirement source, rule/method, applicability condition, obligation, assumption, evidence item, calculation, test result, product declaration and external professional determination.
These form the evidence graph rather than being incidental metadata.
See [Evidence and Provenance](evidence-and-provenance.md).
A relatively small explicit relationship vocabulary is preferable to hundreds of ad-hoc object properties.
The vocabulary should grow from useful cases rather than from exhaustive ontology brainstorming.
The same semantic source can produce several coordinated graphs.
What spaces exist, how are they connected and what hierarchy do they form?
What supports what, where do reactions go and how do gravity/stability relationships close?
Which environmental or safety boundaries exist, where are they continuous and where do they transition or become penetrated?
What supplies what, how do networks connect, and where can systems be isolated or discharged?
How does a person reach a component, where can they work, what must be removed and where does the replacement travel?
What outlives what, what changes together and what slower fabric is touched by a foreseeable intervention?
What proposition applies, what created it, what method addresses it, what evidence supports it and which dependencies can stale it?
> **Semantics create geometric obligations; geometry can discharge some of them.**
Some represented relationships should be invalid or unresolved by construction.
These need not all become programming-language type rules. The principle is simpler:
> **Consequential invalid relationships must be explicit states, not latent facts hidden in drawings.**
The model should keep three categories separate.
Examples: this space has a particular role; this wall uses a selected family; this route is the primary service route; this architectural grammar is selected.
Examples: room area, span, boundary length, roof catchment, opening ratio, collision state or reaction location.
A proposition for which an applicable method and sufficient evidence exist within a declared scope.
The model must represent uncertainty without converting it into certainty.
Assumptions should remain visible and dependency-bearing.
Three ideas should not collapse into one another.
Applicability belongs in the model.
A stable entity can participate in different propositions at different scopes without becoming a “god object” containing permanent fields for every possible analysis.
The roles belong to relationships and contexts rather than inflating the physical noun itself.
The same entity can contribute facts to propositions evaluated at different scales.
Useful scopes can include occurrence, interface, route, room, elevation, system, building and site/target.
Separating contribution from ownership reduces duplicated obligations and incorrect invalidation.
Identical spatial connectivity can have different architectural meaning depending on whether a route is principal arrival, ordinary circulation, service circulation or escape.
The correct model is not four independent checklists that happen to contain similar obligations.
This is the key reason [Interface Obligation Bundles](interface-obligation-bundles.md) are useful as a conceptual authoring abstraction without becoming independent sources of truth.
A future building record may need to distinguish proposed, agreed, manufactured, installed, commissioned, in-service, altered, replaced and removed states.
The ontology should therefore not make temporal identity impossible.
IFC provides valuable precedent for stable identifiers, semantic objects, objectified relationships, spatial structure, system connectivity and analytical views.
It should not automatically dictate the internal ontology.

Some project concepts—maintenance withdrawal volumes, permanence relationships, evidence obligations, architectural grammar—may not map directly to existing exchange schemas. That is an interoperability problem rather than a reason to omit the concepts internally.
These are model invariants, not Ovid’s House doctrine.

The implemented model currently exercises stable identity, source/geometry integrity, spatial relationships, hosted openings, structural topology, service topology, boundary roles/transitions, obligations, scoped evidence and selected versioned numeric methods.
The stop rule remains important: add semantic machinery only when it exposes a real relationship that is otherwise easy to lose, duplicate or misstate.

> **A meaningful architectural relationship contributes facts and constraints to several shared domain graphs, from which canonical obligations are derived.**
Without a higher-level authoring abstraction, a simple operation can create an expert-only forest of consequences.
That creates duplicates and raises an impossible later question: which obligation is the real one?
It should not own authoritative copies of source geometry, product identity or final evidence state.
The same entity can contribute facts to propositions evaluated at several scopes.
These are conceptual scopes rather than a mandatory software enum.
A physical entity should not become a god-object with permanent fields for every possible analysis.

A door can simultaneously be part of ordinary circulation, a selected escape route, an acoustic separation and an architectural hierarchy without those roles becoming intrinsic universal properties of “Door”.
These are different abstractions.
Defines **what the relationship commits the building to resolving**.
Defines **how a bounded physical solution can discharge those obligations**, with geometry, product/system conditions and evidence.
Keeping them separate prevents a detail family from becoming the only imaginable architectural solution and prevents the abstract bundle from pretending it proves physical performance.
Each derived obligation can be supported by evidence appropriate to its authority and scope.
Change should invalidate evidence selectively.
It should not automatically stale an unrelated service penetration elsewhere on the building merely because both belong to the envelope.
The shared dependency graph provides that selectivity.
Pattern provenance and technical validity remain deliberately separable.

The present compiler already exercises the crucial underlying behaviour without requiring a universal runtime “bundle” object: ordinary source relationships feed shared structural, service and boundary semantics; selected crossings generate obligations; evidence remains scoped; and changes propagate through canonical source identity.
See [Formal Architectural Model](formal-architectural-model.md), [Validity and Obligations](validity-and-obligations.md) and [Boundary Semantics](boundary-semantics.md).

> **Can a deliberately bounded, architecturally opinionated domestic design system represent enough shared architectural meaning that consequential changes propagate coherently, invalid states fail clearly and evidence remains scoped—without pretending to automate the whole building?**
Any claim of distinctiveness belongs to that synthesis and its demonstrated behaviour, not to the existence of BIM, ontologies, grammars or rule checking themselves.
Industry Foundation Classes provide an established international model for semantic built-asset information exchange.
The important lesson is that relationships such as support, containment and connection can themselves carry semantics rather than being incidental object attributes.
bSDD demonstrates the value of shared identifiers and definitions across classification systems and IFC concepts.
A dictionary does not by itself provide architectural grammar, proof semantics or a compiler.
buildingSMART’s IDS provides a strong precedent for pairing human-readable information requirements with machine-interpretable constraints and deterministic checking.
The transferable idea is the discipline of explicit, machine-checkable requirements with clear scope and interoperability.
Automated code- and rule-compliance research has a long history. Recent work increasingly emphasises:
This aligns with the project’s insistence that a compliance result cannot be an opaque green tick.

The stronger architectural question is upstream: rather than only checking an arbitrary finished model, can authoring occur inside a semantic system where important consequences are generated as obligations as the design changes?
AEC ontology research spans construction process, cost, operation and maintenance, safety, sustainability, compliance, monitoring and digital twins.
A recurring difficulty is fragmentation: different domains need overlapping views of the same building.
No single graph is the building.
Existing service ontologies distinguish equipment identity, functional networks and physical topology. That is directly relevant to House Kernel.
The additional Ovid’s House concern is maintenance geography: how a human reaches, isolates, services and replaces the system.

The useful contribution is therefore not to reinvent service ontology, but to connect service semantics to spatial access, crossings, boundaries and lifecycle obligations within the same project model.
Shape grammar research established that architectural languages can be represented through generative rules rather than numerical optimisation alone.
Historical examples include grammars for Palladian villas, Frank Lloyd Wright prairie houses, gardens and decorative systems.

This is important because it removes any need to defend “architectural grammar” as a category. The real questions are which relationships deserve formalisation, what authority the rules have and how their limits are made visible.

**Architectural platform** — the enduring combination of fabric, interfaces, maintenance geography, boundary strategy and attachment/service provisions within which faster-changing systems can be maintained, repaired and replaced without repeatedly consuming slower construction.

**Boundary debt** — the performance obligation created when access, services, openings or disassembly interrupt another function of construction: structure, fire, smoke, acoustics, air, vapour, water, thermal continuity, pests or security as applicable.

**Designed interface** — a deliberate junction between assemblies that manages the functions actually present: load transfer, restraint, movement, tolerance, fixing, sealing, drainage, fire/acoustic separation, inspection, disassembly or renewal.

**External maintenance envelope** — the task-specific combination of approach route, supporting ground, working position, clearance, handling space and temporary access needed to inspect, clean, repair or replace an external building element safely.

**Held candidate** — a plausible reusable proposition deliberately kept outside the canonical pattern language because evidence, transfer, proportionality or physical-quality questions remain unresolved.

**Interface infrastructure** — a durable intermediary such as a bearing, rail, mounting frame, backplane, ground or edge condition that allows faster-changing work to attach to slower construction through a controlled relationship.

**Ovidian frame** — the project’s conceptual account of permanence through change: architecture can remain enduring not by resisting every transformation, but by giving necessary transformations deliberate places to occur.

**Physical Service Index** — a small durable in-building record that identifies critical service routes, isolations and system relationships so that essential knowledge survives the loss of digital records.

**Replaceable system** — a service, plant item, control, finish, fitting or other component whose useful life is materially shorter than the slower fabric around it and whose renewal should therefore be anticipated.

**Tolerance strategy** — the explicit account of how constructions of different achievable accuracy meet: controlling datum, expected incoming variation, adjustment capacity, permitted packers/shims or sacrificial elements, acceptance limits and remediation threshold.

**Workmanship robustness** — the ability of a design to tolerate credible construction variation and to make important errors visible and correctable rather than relying on continuous designer interpretation or site improvisation.

**Core doctrine** defines the proposition that would materially change if removed: build for time; preserve slower fabric; design interfaces; plan for failure; give maintenance geography; let permanence remain architectural; and preserve intergenerational legibility.

**Standing architectural disciplines** constrain how that doctrine is allowed to become a house: ordinary parts and understandable assembly; repose; passive-first environmental design; and the architectural resolution of technology.
The constitution operates within non-negotiable requirements for life safety, legal compliance, structural integrity, health and environmental performance.
Longevity does not override whole-life cost, carbon, building physics or construction risk.
**Serviceability is pursued proportionately.** Permanent provision should reflect the frequency, consequence and retrofit difficulty of the future event it is intended to support.

**Do not use long-lived fabric as the routine distribution or attachment zone for shorter-lived systems. Where services, fittings or replaceable assemblies must cross or attach to permanent construction, make those interfaces sparse, deliberate, concentrated where practical and documented.**
**Treat junctions between systems, materials and lifespan layers as designed building elements.**
**Design credible failures to reveal themselves early, remain safely managed and locally containable where practical, and be reachable for repair before they consume long-lived fabric.**
Ask how the system fails, what that failure touches, how it is detected and where it is stopped.
**Organise maintenance-intensive systems, working spaces, access routes, supporting ground and replacement paths as a coherent spatial topology established during design.**
**Prefer widely understood components, standard interfaces and ordinary fabrication methods; concentrate invention in the architectural arrangement and at interfaces that genuinely require it.**

Architecture often ends its story at handover. Drawings describe the building to be made; photographs catch the brief period when it is complete, clean and apparently still. Technical information gathers around the same event. Practical completion becomes the end point.
For a long-lived house, it is the beginning.

From then on the building moves, weathers and wears. Components fail or become obsolete. Bathrooms and kitchens are renewed. New cables and equipment are added. Windows fail while the masonry around them remains sound. Pipes leak, drains block and rooms acquire uses absent from the original brief. This is the ordinary life of a building.
The useful measure is not only how long a component lasts, but how much longer-lived building must be consumed when it moves, fails or is renewed.
> **The permanent architecture should remain stable because change has been given deliberate places to occur.**
The architectural consequences are less consistently pursued, particularly in the ordinary house.

Consider an ordinary fan replacement, a new cable, a leaking washing-machine hose or a failed glazing unit. The questions recur. Can the affected system be identified and isolated? Can a person reach it, disconnect it and withdraw it? Can the replacement arrive without destroying unrelated work? If failure releases water, smoke, dust or noise, where does it go?
The intended result should be quieter than the reasoning that produces it. Rooms may feel solid and permanent precisely because the shorter-lived systems around them have somewhere else to change.
A building does not possess one useful life.

Coupling is therefore not a conceptual step beyond Brand. The move made here is narrower: turn that inherited warning into a domestic intervention test—what sound, slower-lived construction must actually be crossed, damaged or reinstated when the faster thing changes?
> **A component's lifespan matters less than the lifespan of the things that must be destroyed to replace it.**

The principle does not require everything to be exposed or individually demountable. A component expected to last as long as the assembly around it may reasonably be enclosed. Structural crossings may be unavoidable. Bonded finishes may sometimes be the best technical answer. The dependency should be deliberate rather than accidental.
**Long-lived fabric** includes foundations, principal structure, major masonry, primary floor and roof structure and other elements intended to remain substantially undisturbed.
**Renewable architectural elements** include windows, doors, roof coverings, major joinery and other components that may last decades without being permanent.
**Replaceable systems** include plant, pipework, electrical distribution, ventilation equipment, controls and technologies expected to be renewed within the life of the building.
**Fit-out and wear layers** include finishes, fittings, appliances, seals and other components exposed to daily use, fashion or relatively frequent replacement.
The existence of change does not imply infinite flexibility.

Ecology offers a useful distinction. C. S. Holling separated resilience—the capacity to persist through disturbance—from stability understood as remaining near one equilibrium.[28] The architectural analogy is limited but useful: a house can preserve its identity without requiring every technical arrangement to remain fixed.

Permanence is a design commitment, not an automatic virtue. Making something permanent makes it harder to alter and more likely to force future work around it. The question is not only whether an element can be made durable, but whether it benefits from permanence and whether the coupling it creates is justified.

Heraclitus supplies a sharper philosophical analogy. The strongest surviving river fragment describes the same rivers receiving different waters; one influential scholarly reading is that the river remains what it is through the turnover of what it contains.[31] A house is not a river, but the distinction is useful. Material sameness is not the only imaginable form of continuity.

This also suggests a better question than asking which components are literally permanent: **what are the persistence conditions of the house?** In architectural rather than metaphysical terms, which spatial, structural, material, legal or cultural relationships matter enough that their continuity should govern later change? The answer may vary by project and need not be machine-readable.
Longevity is inadequate if the resulting house is exhausting to inhabit.

Repose is a doctrine term, not a clinical construct or a single experimentally measured state.

The word also has architectural ancestry. In 1902 A. S. Wainwright, reporting W. H. That is an architectural antecedent, not a scientific foundation for the doctrine used here.

Structural appearance is a more tentative part of the argument. Vision research indicates that people rapidly infer support, stability, mass and gravity from what they see.[24] That supports a limited architectural review question where structure is conspicuous: is the apparent relationship of support, mass and equilibrium deliberate and intelligible? It does **not** establish that one visual account of equilibrium improves long-duration domestic comfort, that cantilevers are harmful, or that historically familiar support is intrinsically preferable.
The doctrine rejects both a finished object that resists all change and a universal kit of parts in which nothing is allowed to become architecture.
> **Change should be given deliberate places to occur so that architecture can afford to remain permanent elsewhere.**

**Permanent fabric** is the part of the building intended to have the longest useful life and remain substantially undisturbed: foundations, principal structure, major masonry, primary floor and roof structure, and long-lived portions of the envelope.

> **Permanent fabric should not be used as the routine distribution or attachment zone for shorter-lived systems. Unavoidable crossings and attachments should be sparse, deliberate, limited and documented.**

Access should correspond to the work actually expected. A frequently changed filter deserves easier access than an infrequently inspected pipe joint. A major plant item needs a withdrawal route. A service likely to expand may justify spare capacity. Accessibility is graduated rather than binary.
The meeting point between assemblies is where different materials, movements, tolerances and service lives become one constructional problem.
The platform therefore has to accommodate **variation during its making** as well as change after completion.

Between permanent fabric and replaceable systems there may be a limited layer of **interface infrastructure**: bearings, mounting frames, fixing rails, backplanes, edge frames or service carriers that let faster-changing work attach without repeatedly consuming permanent structure.
> **Build the permanent house. Assemble the changeable house inside it.**
Accessible components do not necessarily make a maintainable building.

The alternative is not a completely demountable interior. The proposition is selective:
> **The permanent building should provide a limited number of durable interfaces through which a much larger number of shorter-lived interior assemblies can attach, move and change.**

The question is not whether every interface is hidden, but whether the collection of interfaces produces a coherent domestic field. This book is an attempt to give change its own architecture: not a house that changes continually, but a house able to remain itself because the things that must change have been given somewhere else to go.

The name **Ovid’s House** came late to this enquiry. Ovid’s *Metamorphoses* is a poem of altered forms, but the connection is not that Roman poetry contains a concealed theory of building. It does not. The useful affinity is narrower: transformation repeatedly makes identity a question. What has changed, what remains, and when has one thing become another?[5]

Architecture usually meets that question without magic. A boiler is replaced. Wiring is renewed. A window reaches the end of its useful life. A room accepts another use. Roof coverings, controls and finishes disappear while structure and spatial order continue. Over a sufficiently long life, a house can become materially different from the thing first handed over while remaining, in ordinary architectural and cultural terms, the same house.

Nor is transformation automatically good. In Ovid it is often violent, punitive or irreversible. In buildings too, change can destroy as easily as renew. The task is not to celebrate change. It is to decide what should endure, what should be allowed to change, and how necessary change can occur without needlessly consuming the rest.

Permanence, then, need not mean stasis. A house may remain itself not by refusing transformation, but by making some transformations ordinary enough that what matters can persist through them. That is the sense in which this is **Ovid’s House**.

Repose begins with a simple question: how much attention does the building require from the people living in it? Some answers are measurable.
